/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Temporal
  The temporal operators over a whole trace at once: every operator maps per-instant arrays to a
  per-instant array in one pass (or one pass plus O(1) window queries), so a formula costs
  O(|φ| · n log n) per grounding. Semantics and Derived both use these; nothing here knows what
  a formula or a road user is.

  Finite-trace policy: the unobserved past and future are unknown (`windowTruncated`), never a
  verdict. A lookback window must be covered and adequately sampled; a lookahead window is true
  on a witness, false only when covered.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Time
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Unknown

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Temporal

def const (n : Nat) (r : R) : Array R := Array.replicate n r
def truncated (op : String) : R := R.u (.windowTruncated op)

-- pointwise connectives
def zipAnd (a b : Array R) : Array R := Array.zipWith R.and a b
def zipOr (a b : Array R) : Array R := Array.zipWith R.or a b
def zipImplies (a b : Array R) : Array R := Array.zipWith R.implies a b
def mapNot (a : Array R) : Array R := a.map R.not
def allOf (n : Nat) (xs : List (Array R)) : Array R := xs.foldl zipAnd (const n R.t)
def anyOf (n : Nat) (xs : List (Array R)) : Array R := xs.foldl zipOr (const n R.f)

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Unbounded operators: one backward or forward pass with the unobserved tail as unknown.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
private def backward (tail : R) (step : R → R → R) (vals : Array R) : Array R :=
  let n := vals.size
  ((List.range n).reverse.foldl (fun (acc : Array R × R) i =>
    let r := step vals[i]! acc.2
    (acc.1.set! i r, r)) (Array.replicate n tail, tail)).1

private def forward (head : R) (step : R → R → R) (vals : Array R) : Array R :=
  let n := vals.size
  ((List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array R × R) i =>
    let r := step vals[i]! acc.2
    (acc.1.set! i r, r)) (Array.replicate n head, head)).1

/-- `always φ`: φ here and at every later observation, and the unobserved future. -/
def alwaysAll (φ : Array R) : Array R := backward (truncated "always") R.and φ
/-- `eventually φ`: φ here or later, or the unobserved future. -/
def eventuallyAll (φ : Array R) : Array R := backward (truncated "eventually") R.or φ
/-- Strong until: `ψ ∨ (φ ∧ until')`, the unobserved future as the tail. -/
def untilAll (φ ψ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let n := ψ.size
  ((List.range n).reverse.foldl (fun (acc : Array R × R) i =>
    let r := R.or ψ[i]! (R.and φ[i]! acc.2)
    (acc.1.set! i r, r)) (Array.replicate n (truncated "until"), truncated "until")).1
/-- Since: `ψ ∨ (φ ∧ since')`, the unobserved past as the head. -/
def sinceAll (φ ψ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let n := ψ.size
  ((List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array R × R) i =>
    let r := R.or ψ[i]! (R.and φ[i]! acc.2)
    (acc.1.set! i r, r)) (Array.replicate n (truncated "since"), truncated "since")).1
/-- `once φ`: φ here or at some earlier observation, or the unobserved past. -/
def onceAll (φ : Array R) : Array R := forward (truncated "once") (fun v acc => R.or v acc) φ
/-- φ at the previous observation (`first` at the trace start). -/
def prevAll (first : R) (φ : Array R) : Array R :=
  (Array.range φ.size).map fun i => if i = 0 then first else φ[i - 1]!

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Metric windows: positions per instant (time or path), a length d, per-instant values.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- φ at every observation in the window of length `d` behind each instant. Unknown where a
    position inside the window is missing; where the window is not covered, false on a false
    already observed inside it and unknown otherwise; unknown where it is covered but not
    adequately sampled. -/
def holdsForAll (pos : Array (Option Q)) (d : Q) (op : String) (missing : UnknownReason) (φ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let wins := Time.backWindows pos d
  let agg := RangeAgg.build φ
  (Array.range φ.size).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => R.u missing
    | some w =>
      if !w.covered then (if (agg.all w.j0 i).v = .f then R.f else truncated op)
      else if !w.adequate then R.u (.samplingGap op)
      else agg.all w.j0 i

/-- The value of φ at the latest observation `j` in `[j0, i]` at which ψ held: unknown where ψ is
    unknown at an observation later than any at which it held; none where ψ held nowhere in the range. -/
private def atLastAt (ψ φ : Array R) (j0 i : Nat) : Option R :=
  (List.range (i + 1 - j0)).foldl (fun (acc : Option R) k =>
    match acc with
    | some r => some r
    | none =>
      let j := i - k
      match ψ[j]!.v with
      | .t => some φ[j]!
      | .u => some ⟨.u, ψ[j]!.why⟩
      | .f => none) none

/-- φ at the last observation in the window of length `d` behind each instant at which ψ held.
    Unknown where a position is missing, where ψ is unknown later than any observation at which it
    held, where the window is not adequately sampled (an unobserved later instant could be the last
    one at which ψ held), and where ψ held nowhere in a window that is not covered; false where ψ
    held nowhere in a covered, adequately sampled window. -/
def atLastAll (pos : Array (Option Q)) (d : Q) (op : String) (missing : UnknownReason) (ψ φ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let wins := Time.backWindows pos d
  (Array.range φ.size).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => R.u missing
    | some w =>
      match atLastAt ψ φ w.j0 i with
      | some r => if !w.adequate then R.u (.samplingGap op) else r
      | none => if !w.covered then truncated op else if !w.adequate then R.u (.samplingGap op) else R.f

/-- φ at some observation in the window of length `d` ahead: true on a witness, false only when
    the window is covered, unknown when it runs off the trace. -/
def withinAll (pos : Array (Option Q)) (d : Q) (op : String) (missing : UnknownReason) (φ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let wins := Time.forwardWindows pos d
  let agg := RangeAgg.build φ
  (Array.range φ.size).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => R.u missing
    | some w =>
      if !w.adequate then R.u (.samplingGap op)
      else
        let a := agg.any i w.jl
        if w.covered then a else R.or a (truncated op)

/-- Smallest `k ≥ i` whose value satisfies `p` (size when none), per instant. -/
def nextWhere (vals : Array R) (p : Tri → Bool) : Array Nat :=
  let n := vals.size
  (List.range n).reverse.foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i =>
    acc.set! i (if p vals[i]!.v then i else acc[i + 1]!)) (Array.replicate (n + 1) n)

/-- Strong until restricted to the window ahead: ∃ j in the window, ψ at j and φ at every
    observation from here to just before j; the unobserved remainder counts as unknown unless φ
    already failed. -/
def untilWithinAll (pos : Array (Option Q)) (d : Q) (op : String) (missing : UnknownReason) (φ ψ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let wins := Time.forwardWindows pos d
  let aggφ := RangeAgg.build φ
  let aggψ := RangeAgg.build ψ
  let firstψ := nextWhere ψ (· = .t)
  let firstφf := nextWhere φ (· = .f)
  (Array.range φ.size).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => R.u missing
    | some w =>
      if !w.adequate then R.u (.samplingGap op)
      else
        let b := firstψ[i]!
        -- φ at every observation from i up to, not including, b (empty when b = i)
        let φBefore (b : Nat) : R := if b ≤ i then R.t else aggφ.all i (b - 1)
        let witnessed : R :=
          if b ≤ w.jl && (φBefore b).v = .t then R.t
          else
            -- false only if every candidate fails: ψ false up to the first φ failure (or the window end)
            let a := firstφf[i]!
            let hi := min a w.jl
            let ψany := aggψ.any i hi
            if ψany.v = .f then R.f
            else
              let why := (if ψany.v = .u then ψany.why else []) ++
                (if b ≤ w.jl then (φBefore b).why else [])
              ⟨.u, if why.isEmpty then [.windowTruncated op] else why⟩
        if w.covered then witnessed
        else R.or witnessed (R.and (truncated op) (aggφ.all i w.jl))

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Runs and counts
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- The first instant of the latest run of true values ending at the latest true instant ≤ i:
    "since φ became true". `none` before any true; an error where an unknown value hides the
    run's start, and `windowTruncated op` where the run reaches the trace start (it may have
    begun before the recording). -/
def runStartAll (op : String) (vals : Array R) : Array (Except UnknownReason (Option Nat)) :=
  let n := vals.size
  ((List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array (Except UnknownReason (Option Nat)) × Except UnknownReason (Option Nat)) i =>
    let v := vals[i]!
    let st : Except UnknownReason (Option Nat) :=
      match v.v with
      | .t =>
        if i = 0 then .error (.windowTruncated op)
        else match vals[i - 1]!.v with
          | .t => acc.2
          | .f => .ok (some i)
          | .u => .error (vals[i - 1]!.why.head?.getD (.malformed op))
      | .f => acc.2
      | .u => .error (v.why.head?.getD (.malformed op))
    (acc.1.push st, st)) (Array.mkEmpty n, .ok none)).1

/-- Path length over which `holds` has held continuously up to each instant: zero where it does
    not hold, unknown where it is unknown, where the path length is missing, or where the run
    reaches the trace start. -/
def distanceWhileAll (pathPos : Array (Option Q)) (holds : Array R) : Array QR :=
  let starts := runStartAll "distance_while" holds
  (Array.range holds.size).map fun i =>
    match holds[i]!.v with
    | .f => .ok Q.zero
    | .u => .error (holds[i]!.why.head?.getD (.malformed "distance_while"))
    | .t =>
      match starts[i]! with
      | .error e => .error e
      | .ok none => .error (.windowTruncated "distance_while")

/-- Zero, the sign threshold of the components and of the overlap. -/
def zero : Term := .lit Q.zero .metre

def pos (x : Arg) (c : String) : Term := .measure "kin_position" [x, .lit c]
def hdg (x : Arg) (c : String) : Term := .measure "kin_heading" [x, .lit c]

/-- The longitudinal component, along a's heading (kin.heading), of the vector from a's position
    to b's position (kin.position). -/
def lon : Term :=
  .add (.mul (hdg aA "x") (.sub (pos aB "x") (pos aA "x")))
       (.mul (hdg aA "y") (.sub (pos aB "y") (pos aA "y")))

/-- The shared length of the two bodies' projections on a's heading. -/
def overlap : Term := .measure "rel_longitudinal_overlap" [aA, aB]

/-- b ahead of a: longitudinal component positive, projections sharing no length. -/
def ahead : Formula := .and (.cmp lon .gt zero) (.cmp overlap .lt zero)

/-- Headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction). -/
def aligned : Formula := .atom "rel_same_direction" [aA, aB] [pSameDirCos]

/-- b ahead of a with their headings aligned: the observation at which the act begins is the last
    such one. -/
def aheadAligned : Formula := .and ahead aligned

/-- The two side by side: the projections on a's heading share length (overlap at or above zero). -/
def sideBySide : Formula := .cmp overlap .ge zero

/-- b on a's left: the lateral component of b's bearing in a's frame is positive. -/
def onLeft : Formula := .atom "rel_bearing" [aA, aB, .lit "left"] []

/-- b on a's left at every observation since the act began at which the two are side by side. -/
def leftWhileAlongside : Formula := .since (.implies sideBySide onLeft) aheadAligned

/-- drv.interaction.overtake_pass holds for a and b (same window, same tolerance), with b on a's
    left there and at every side-by-side observation since the act began. -/
def body : Formula :=
  .and (.derived "drv_interaction_overtake_pass" [aA, aB] [pWindow, pSameDirCos])
    (.and onLeft leftWhileAlongside)

# drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right — task result

## Final verdict
**OK** (gate run 1 of 6): 3 witnesses, 6 names, reads 6 atoms.

## Gate runs
1. `OK` — first run, on the body and witnesses described below. Nothing changed after it.

## Body
`overtake_pass(a, b; window, same_dir_cos) ∧ onLeft ∧ since (sideBySide → onLeft) aheadAligned`
- `onLeft` = `rel_bearing a b "left"` (the lateral component of b's bearing is positive).
- `sideBySide` = `rel_longitudinal_overlap a b ≥ 0`.
- `aheadAligned` = `lon > 0 ∧ overlap < 0 ∧ rel_same_direction a b [same_dir_cos]`. Here `lon` is the
  component of b's position minus a's position along a's heading (`kin_heading`, `kin_position`),
  computed the same way `overtake_pass` computes it.
- `since` is ψ ∨ (φ ∧ previous). It therefore reaches back to the latest observation where b was
  ahead with the headings aligned. That observation is the act's onset, and `overtake_pass`
  requires it to lie in the window. The recognition, the extent ("not again until…") and the
  history limit all come from `overtake_pass`.

## Choices the record left open
None needed a narrowing. The words map directly onto the operators: "at every observation since
the act began at which the two are side by side" becomes `since` with an implication.

## Note for the plan agent (the blind scenario)
In Core, a computed `rel.bearing` is `relFrame`, built from `kin.position` and `kin.heading`.
Masking `rel.bearing` only drops a *measured* bearing. When the positions and headings are
observed (and `overtake_pass` needs them at the recognition), the side is always computable. So
the narrative as written ("rel.bearing not observed … the side … there and while side by side
cannot be read") cannot be realised at the recognition instant.

How the blind witness reaches unknown:
- Its source loses the positions while the two are side by side (k5–k7) and measures the bearing
  and the overlap on the relation instead.
- Core cannot compute either value there, so supplying them is allowed.
- `overtake_pass` does not need positions at side-by-side observations, because the measured
  overlap already decides that b is neither ahead nor behind.
- With `rel.bearing` masked, the side-by-side part of the condition is unknown, and the only
  reason given is the bearing that was dropped. With the bearing observed, the trace is the
  compliant pass.

The gate accepted this. A future record that needs a bearing-blind witness should expect it to
work only where the positions are not observed.

## Why I finished
The gate returned OK.

The gate accepted the concept on the first of the six allowed runs: it returned `OK` for all three witnesses, and I used no narrowings.

**How the concept is written** (`library/TrafficSpec/Concepts/interaction/overtake_pass_on_right.lean`):
- It calls `drv.interaction.overtake_pass` for a and b with the same `window` and `same_dir_cos`. That concept already covers when the pass is recognised, holding only once until b is ahead again, and not reading before the window.
- It adds that b is on a's left at the recognition (`rel_bearing … "left"`).
- It also requires b on a's left at every observation since the act began where the two are side by side (`rel_longitudinal_overlap ≥ 0`). This is written as a `since` that runs back to the last observation where b was ahead of a with headings aligned, which is the act's onset.

**Witnesses** (`library/TrafficSpecWitness/Concepts/interaction/overtake_pass_on_right.lean`):
- **Setup:** b is halted at (100, 0) facing east. a follows in the same lane, moves sideways 4 m, draws alongside b and clears it. Every scenario is judged at 8000 ms, when b first falls behind a. The window is 6 s and `same_dir_cos` is 9/10.
- **holds:** a moves to the right, so b is on a's left throughout and the concept holds.
- **fails:** a moves to the left, so b is on a's right; `overtake_pass` still holds but this concept does not.

**Problem with the record's blind scenario:** Core works out `rel.bearing` from the same positions and heading that `overtake_pass` needs. Masking `rel.bearing` only removes a bearing the source measured itself. So the narrative's version, where only the bearing is missing, cannot actually produce unknown.

What I built instead:
- The blind source has no positions while the two vehicles are side by side (k5–k7), and measures the bearing and the overlap directly there.
- Core can't compute either value at those observations, so supplying them breaks no witness rule.
- `overtake_pass` doesn't need positions there, because the overlap alone shows b is neither ahead nor behind.
- With the bearing masked, the result is unknown for that reason alone. With it unmasked, it's the compliant pass.

The gate accepted this. I explained it in `task_result.md` as a note for the plan agent, but did not report the record as wrong.
